arguments.summary: A critical firewall integrity breach was discovered following an alert on suspicious activity from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). Investigation revealed that the host was compromised via a malicious PowerShell script used to deploy Cobalt Strike beaconing to a known C2 server. The attacker exploited CVE-2026-21884 (PAN-OS Rule Corruption) to inject corrupted inbound ACL rules on the primary perimeter firewall (10.0.1.1), allowing unauthorized access on high-risk ports including 445, 3389, and 8443. The firewall's rule set is now considered fully compromised, requiring a complete rebuild from a known-good backup. The source of initial compromise appears to be a phishing email leading to execution of encoded PowerShell from Outlook. No evidence of data exfiltration was found during this phase, but lateral movement attempts were detected.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Config {
    meta:
        description = "Detects embedded configuration in Cobalt Strike beacons"
        author = "SOC Threat Intel"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        tlp = "amber"
        malpedia_reference = "https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.cobalt_strike"
    strings:
        $a = { 2e 72 63 64 2e 63 66 67 } // ".rcd.cfg"
        $b = { 68 74 74 70 3a 2f 2f [0-256] 2f 63 6f 6c 6c 65 63 74 6f 72 } // "http://*/collector"
        $c = { 63 6f 62 61 6c 74 73 74 72 69 6b 65 } // "cobaltstrike"
    condition:
        all of ($a, $b, $c)
}

arguments.summary: A high-severity emergency access request was triggered from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to WS-IT-101 (10.0.8.200). Investigation revealed that the source IP 10.0.5.14 was associated with Cobalt Strike beaconing activity originating from WS-FIN-042. The host exhibited suspicious process execution (rundll32 from Temp), C2 communication to an external IP (198.51.100.23), failed Kerberos authentication attempts, and lateral movement via SMB. Although the initial alert referenced IP 10.0.5.14, forensic correlation identified 10.0.5.42 as the actual compromised host. Immediate firewall rules were enacted to block all traffic to and from 10.0.5.14 (likely a misattribution or proxy), but direct host isolation failed due to tooling constraints. The sandbox analysis of the payload returned 'clean', indicating possible evasion techniques.
